messages:
maria: FYI I'm seeing recurring 413s + huge queuing for the embeddings endpoint when customers send big mixed-dim arrays. Happened twice in prod this morning. Dump attached (small redacted):
```
  POST /v1/embeddings 200 items, mixed dims 768/1536, payload ~18MB
  splitter logged: waiting for dim-match window (200ms) before flushing
  batcher queue len spiked to 1200
  413 on response from shard A
```

aj: Is this from the new preflight + dim-splitting flow or the legacy splitter? Any tenant affinity?

maria: It's the preflight-enabled route (route id r-emb-v2). Tenant is a heavy ingest customer, but we've also seen at lower volumes. Looks like the scheduler is waiting for compatible items and holding up everything.

kevin: This matches what I repro'd in staging. The scheduler's `max_wait_ms` heuristic is too aggressive for mixed-dim workloads: it tries to coalesce by dim, ends up holding small items for long tails of incompatible dims. When the queue hits memory threshold we attempt a partial flush but the framing code assumed full-compat batches and returns 413 on the shard-side because framing header length > shard limit.

sasha: Two quick ideas: 1) add an escape hatch where if queue_time > X ms we forcibly flush partial batches with a `partial=true` envelope and let shard handle partial assembly; 2) surface a console metric `embed.fragmentation.blocked_by_dim` and a per-route histogram `embed.partial_flush_rate` so product can see impact.

aj: I like the metric idea. But forcing partial batches might break some downstream invariants (ordering, dedupe). Any way to signal clients? Could expose a header `X-Embed-Partial-Supported: true` that clients/SDKs opt into.

kevin: Agreed on opt-in. Implementation proposal: scheduler adds `Prefer-Partial: true` flag in preflight response when we detect high fragmentation and we're in opt-in rollout. Shard runtime treats `Prefer-Partial` by accepting smaller frames and returning `partial_accepted` telemetry. Also add a soft-fail path: if shard rejects due to framing, we fall back to chunk-by-size (split large payloads into smaller frames) rather than 413.

maria: That fallback sounds safer. We should also consider cost impact (more requests and CPU). Need GA-safe defaults: disabled by default, enabled per-tenant via console toggle, with rollout % and kill-switch.

sasha: For console UX: add a toggle on the route config panel "Enable partial embed flush (opt-in)" with a rollout slider and sample size. Also expose realtime signal charts: queue length, blocked_by_dim, partial_flush_rate, partial_reject_rate. Ideally add a per-tenant trace link that shows exact items held in queue and dims distribution.

aj: Small SDK ask: surface a client header `X-Embed-Prefer-Partial` that we send in client lib when user sets `allow_partial: true`. Server will respect it only if tenant is opted-in. Backwards compatible because default is false.

kevin: Telemetry: add tags on existing spans: `embed.split_strategy=dim|size|partial`, `embed.queue_time_ms`, `embed.fragmentation_ratio`. That will let us build Sankey-style dashboards to show when dim-splitting causes head-of-line blocking.

maria: Ops concern: we need a rate limit policy for partial flushes so we don't amplify request counts. Suggest `partial_rate_limit = min(5% of route RPS, 100 rps)`. Also adapt quota accounting so tokens count the same whether partial or full.

sasha: Rollout plan draft: 1) add telemetry + console signals (1 week) 2) implement opt-in header + server soft-fallback (2 weeks) 3) enable opt-in for small set of tenants + run load tests (1 week) 4) iterate on rate limits and console UX, then expand (ongoing).

aj: One more edge: client-side retries. If we start returning partial-ish 2xxs or structured responses, SDK should prefer streaming/aggregation instead of blind retries to avoid duplicate billing. We'll need SDK changes and docs.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled for emb-scheduler-service v2.14 at 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z for 5% traffic to selected tenants.

maria: OK actionable items: (A) kevin: prototype soft-fallback + telemetry tags (ticket #ENG-1189) due EOW; (B) sasha: console charts + toggle UX (ticket #PRODUCT-634) due next Wed; (C) aj: SDK header + client behavior doc (ticket #DEVEX-410) due next Wed; (D) ops: add quota guard and rate-limit policy (ticket #SRE-271) due in 2 weeks. I'll open the tickets and assign. Thanks all :thumbsup:
